blockers.title: AL-3 sends core-release rollback to a contract and gate that expressly exclude core rollback
blockers.subjectEvidence: AL-3 requires either the coreReleaseIdentity or componentReleaseIdentity to roll back while the counterpart bytes remain unchanged. executionRoutes then sends AL-3 without a split to lifecycle-generation-contract.v2 / D-107 and DR-G18 and declares it 'Not G21'; conformanceModel simultaneously declares DESIGN-ANSWERED and says execution is condition 4 on named gates.
blockers.refutingMeasurement: The consumed lifecycle-generation-contract.v2 bytes at the D-107-recorded digest a5f9d6a35f83d64687cdd2a00ec3106251ae407e54a5538727c086dd8f9ab77b draw the opposite boundary. generationVsSelfUpdateBoundary says G18 generation rollback restores a verified generation pointer, while self-update/repair rollback replaces core bytes and belongs to DR-110 / G08-repair / G11. Its thisArtifactDoesNot says it does not design self-update, repair media, or core replacement, and g18FaultSet.scopeRider says the G18 harness is not self-update rollback. Live file 08 at the subject's pinned digest likewise gives DR-110 to core self-update/repair/rollback and gives DR-G18 to lifecycle-generation recovery.
blockers.counterexample: A system can pass the D-107/G18 generation-pointer rollback and coexistence corpus for component closures, yet have no way to replace or roll back the independently versioned core bytes while leaving the component publication set and selected component identity unchanged. Every routed G18 record passes, but the core half of AL-3 is untested.
blockers.impact: The DR-127 acceptance cell explicitly requires independent core and component rollback. A route whose own accepted contract disclaims core replacement cannot discharge that half, so the claimed DESIGN-ANSWERED standing and the claimed full repair of ALCV2-B2 are false.
blockers.requiredRepair: Split AL-3 by identity. Keep component/generation-selection rollback under the accepted D-107 contract and DR-G18. Route core-release-byte rollback through a reviewed DR-110 owning contract and its applicable named gates, or leave that core half explicitly at DR-127 pending such a reviewed owner/route. Pin the consumed authority and claim no SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, or implementation-authorized standing.

shouldFix.title: The conditional G16 example does not support the blanket condition-4 standing
shouldFix.measurement: At required HEAD 2d5f15b, live file 08 names harness.DR-G16.ci-isolation-integration as not authored and not QUALIFIED, and the pinned current COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md contains no adopted contract for DR-121/G16. The subject correctly conditions any G16 ride on an accepted contract's actual coverage and therefore leaves the AL-1/AL-2/AL-5 remainder at DR-127. It then incorrectly appends '/ condition 4' to that row remainder and declares without qualification that execution is condition 4 on named gates.
shouldFix.governingConflict: D-056 permits an execution remainder to move to condition 4 only when it is already named at a condition-4 DR-G* obligation with an owner. DR-127 is a condition-2 architecture row, not a gate; a contingent 'such as DR-G16' whose accepted coverage is currently absent does not name the remainder at that gate.
shouldFix.whyShouldFix: Unlike v2's wrong wholesale G21 assignment, v3 does not silently misassign these cases and does keep the uncovered remainder at the owning row, so the conformance definitions remain usable as a candidate. But the blanket DESIGN-ANSWERED/condition-4 sentence overstates the current route and could be misread as D-056 eligibility.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: State that uncovered AL-1/AL-2/AL-5 execution remains at DR-127 and is not yet a condition-4 remainder pending a reviewed owning-gate contract, or pin an accepted owning contract and enumerate the exact covered cases. Do not claim D-056 eligibility, SATISFIED, or QUALIFIED.
